title: Osiris: two kingdoms
variant: Plutarch-derived chest and recovery tradition, with Horus succeeding as living king; details vary among tellings.
sentences: Seth murdered his brother for a throne, but Osiris would become ruler of the dead.
In this telling of the Egyptian myth, Osiris ruled alongside Isis, while Seth envied his brother's power.
At a feast, Seth opened a magnificent chest, promising it to whoever fitted inside.
Seth slammed the lid shut, sealed the chest, and threw it into the Nile.
Isis searched for her husband and recovered his body.
Seth later cut the body into pieces and scattered them across Egypt.
Isis gathered the remains and restored Osiris through magic.
Their son Horus would become his father's heir.
Osiris became ruler of the underworld, while Horus grew up to challenge Seth.
Horus defeated Seth and claimed the throne of Egypt.
Seth had tried to end his brother's reign; instead, Osiris ruled the dead, and his son ruled the living.
